tests_required: reserved-name test; long-path test above 260 characters; a control asserting the walk does NOT silently swallow the exception and return zero entries.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Case-distinct key collision detector for configuration documents
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11310 (case-insensitive parser collision on case-distinct JSON keys). Implement the detector that finds two keys differing only by case in any shipped config or manifest, before a case-insensitive consumer silently drops one. Exact question: how many such collisions exist across the shipped configuration surface today?
evidence_requirement: Collision list with file, both keys, and the value each holds; a zero result must be accompanied by a planted-collision control proving the detector fires.
tests_required: planted-collision control; nested-object coverage test; a control asserting keys that differ by more than case are not reported.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Stale-branch reversion guard on the commit-to-commit surface
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11322 (stale branch would revert newer work). Implement the guard that measures the three-dot commit-to-commit diff against the integration base before any proposal is offered, and blocks when the surface contains mass deletions the branch did not author. Exact question: how many deletions does this branch propose, and how many of them are files it never touched?
evidence_requirement: Three-dot diff stat with files changed and deletions, alongside the two-dot number, showing they differ - the two-dot form folds in working-tree noise and is not the proposal surface.
tests_required: stale-branch fixture must be blocked; a freshly-based branch must pass (both-states). A control asserting the guard reads the three-dot form specifically.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer recomputes both diff forms
retry_policy: no automatic retry; a mass-deletion proposal must reach a human

title: Semantic-role detector library replacing payload-text matching
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11323 (false-positive prose and fixture detectors). Implement the shared library that classifies a match by its semantic ROLE - the tool-input verb, the JSON field, the AST position - rather than by the presence of a string in the payload, since a document describing a defect necessarily contains that defect's text. Exact question: on the historical false-positive corpus, what is the before-and-after false-positive rate?
evidence_requirement: Confusion matrix before and after on the historical corpus, with each surviving false positive shown as the raw record so the role-versus-text distinction is visible.
tests_required: mention corpus (documents quoting a dangerous command) must produce zero fires; use corpus (actual invocation) must produce a fire on every entry. A library passing only one of the two corpora is not a fix.
reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter constructs a mention that the library still fires on and a use it misses
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Both-states detector-validation harness applied to every shipped detector
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11324 (detector silent in both broken and fixed states). Implement the harness that, for every shipped detector, runs it against a known-BROKEN and a known-GOOD state and requires it to differ. Exact question: how many of the shipped detectors are silent in BOTH states and therefore measure nothing?
evidence_requirement: Per-detector two-state table: broken-state output, good-state output, and a DIFFERS verdict. Every detector with no known-broken fixture is NOT-CHECKED, not passing.
tests_required: the harness needs its own control: a detector known to be two-state-valid must be reported valid, and a deliberately inert stub detector must be reported as measuring nothing.
reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter selects three detectors and constructs independent broken states
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Per-session process-multiplication guard for MCP-style child processes
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11326 (eager per-session MCP process multiplication). Implement the guard that measures live child-process count per session and refuses to start a new session tier that would push the machine past its process budget, preferring a shared long-lived service over per-session duplication. Exact question: what is the current processes-per-session multiplier, measured from the process table?
evidence_requirement: Measured multiplier from the process table (processes divided by sessions), and the configuration scope each server is actually enabled at - a setting present at the wrong scope is inert and must be shown to be inert, not assumed effective.
tests_required: scope test asserting the guard reads the scope that actually takes effect; budget test asserting a new tier is refused at the ceiling. Control: the guard must still permit startup below the ceiling.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer verifies the effective scope from the process table, not from the config file
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Shared-service protection in the resource guard's termination path
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11328 (kill-based memory guard terminates a live shared service). Implement an allowlist plus a proof-of-orphan requirement so the resource guard can only terminate a process it has proven to be an orphan of a dead session. Exact target: a live shared service must be unkillable by the guard even at the memory ceiling.
evidence_requirement: A ceiling-pressure run in which a shared service is present and survives, with the guard's per-candidate decision record showing why it was spared.
tests_required: shared-service-survives test at the ceiling; orphan-is-reaped test; a mutation removing the allowlist must kill the shared service and turn the first test red.
reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus owner approval, because this guard can terminate the owner's running services
retry_policy: no automatic retry; a wrong termination takes down a live service

title: Rollback contract that cannot remove existing commands or user data
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11347 (rollback removes existing commands or user data). Implement rollback as an additive-restore with a pre-rollback inventory and a post-rollback diff, so any command or user-data path present before and absent after is a hard failure. Exact question: what is the set difference of available commands and user-data paths across a real rollback, and is it empty?
evidence_requirement: Before-and-after inventories with the computed set difference for both commands and user-data paths; a rollback rehearsal that was never actually executed is NOT-CHECKED, not passing.
tests_required: rollback rehearsal on a disposable profile; a planted user-data file must survive; a mutation making rollback destructive must turn the test red.
reviewer_requirement: 2 independent reviewers plus owner approval before rollback is exercised against a real profile
retry_policy: no automatic retry; re-running a destructive rollback compounds the loss

title: Marketplace package permission scanner for excessive and malicious grants
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11346 (marketplace package has malicious or excessive permissions). Implement the scanner that compares a package's declared permissions against the minimum its code actually exercises, and flags every grant with no corresponding use. Exact question: for each fixture package, which declared permissions are never exercised by its code?
evidence_requirement: Per-package declared-versus-exercised permission table with the code anchor for each exercised permission; an unexercised grant with no anchor is the finding.
tests_required: malicious fixture package (over-broad grants plus an exfiltration path) must be flagged; a minimal well-scoped package must NOT be flagged (both-states).
reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus a cross-vendor codex reviewer on the malicious fixture
retry_policy: max 3 attempts for batch transients; zero retries on a scanner that flags every package

title: Health-check command built on two-signal probes only
question_or_target: Implement the health-check command so every reported status is backed by two mechanically independent probes, and any single-probe check reports NOT-CHECKED rather than OK. Exact question: how many of the health checks can currently produce a green verdict from one probe alone?
evidence_requirement: Per-check listing of BOTH probes with their outputs; a check declaring only one probe is a violation and must render as NOT-CHECKED in the report.
tests_required: single-probe check must render NOT-CHECKED; a two-probe check with disagreeing probes must render DISAGREE, never OK. Positive control on a genuinely healthy component.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer audits three checks for genuine probe independence
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Versioned schema migration engine with a launcher freeze marker
question_or_target: Implement the migration engine required by spec line 10660 - once the first implementation wave starts, launchers and schemas are frozen and any change requires a versioned migration. Exact target: an in-place schema edit after the freeze marker is set must be refused, and the only accepted path is a numbered migration with an executable down-step.
evidence_requirement: A refused in-place edit after the freeze, and an accepted migration with its up and down steps both executed against a fixture corpus.
tests_required: freeze test (in-place edit refused); round-trip test (up then down restores the original bytes); a migration with no down-step must be refused.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer executes the down-step independently
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Actionable error catalog covering every failure class
question_or_target: Implement the user-facing error catalog mapping every class in the failure taxonomy to a message that names what failed, why, and the exact next command. Exact question: how many taxonomy classes currently have no user-facing message, and after this unit is that number zero?
evidence_requirement: Coverage table: taxonomy class, message id, and the next command it recommends. Every recommended command must be executed verbatim by the documentation test.
tests_required: coverage test asserting zero unmapped classes; documentation-command test executing every recommended next command; a control asserting a class added later is reported as unmapped.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer runs three messages end to end as a naive user
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s

title: Telemetry and privacy contract implementation with an executable redaction proof
question_or_target: Implement the telemetry and privacy contract from spec line 10819: what is recorded, what is redacted, where it is stored, how it is disabled. Exact target: redaction must be proven executably against planted canaries - a policy document is not an implementation, and an ephemeral channel is not exfiltration-safe.
evidence_requirement: Canary sweep results across every emission point: planted secret-shaped token, planted absolute home path, planted project name - each must be absent from the emitted stream, with the emission point named.
tests_required: canary test per emission point; opt-out test asserting disabling telemetry emits literally nothing; a control proving the sweep can detect a canary that was NOT redacted.
reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus owner approval of the recorded-field list
retry_policy: no automatic retry on a canary leak; escalate with the blast-radius trace

title: Prompt-injection defence on the artifact-consumption boundary
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11344 (an artifact injects instructions into a later stage). Implement the boundary that treats every consumed artifact - transcripts, fetched pages, peer results, participant outputs - as untrusted DATA, never as instructions, with a structural wrapper rather than a prompt-level plea. Exact question: does a planted instruction inside an artifact change the behavior of the consuming stage?
evidence_requirement: Behavioral diff for each planted injection: consuming-stage output with and without the injection present. Identical outputs are the pass condition; any divergence names the injection that worked.
tests_required: injection corpus covering role-spoof, ignore-previous-instructions, encoded payload, and a credential-read request; every one must produce an identical downstream output. Control: a benign artifact edit that SHOULD change the output must change it, proving the diff is sensitive.
reviewer_requirement: security reviewer plus an adversarial refuter who authors three new injections the corpus has never seen
retry_policy: no automatic retry on a successful injection; escalate and widen the corpus
